Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- Policy stance: Hold at 5.25–5.50% and “greater confidence” in disinflation required before cuts = hawkish signal. QT pace slowed via lower Treasury redemption caps = dovish technical tweak.
- SLOOS lens: Banks report tighter standards and terms across C&I and consumer credit (credit cards, auto), wider spreads, higher credit score requirements, and weaker loan demand. CRE standards remain notably tighter, with banks citing vacancy rates, rents, and property prices. These point to ongoing endogenous tightening in credit conditions that should restrain growth and inflation without additional rate hikes.
- Implication: SLOOS-driven credit headwinds and QT slowdown temper the statement’s hawkish inflation language. Net tone shifts from slightly hawkish to near-neutral with only a marginal hawkish tilt.
